intro: Professionals and everyday users convert cups (us) (cup) to milliliters (mL) when working across us_customary and metric standards in culinary recipe scaling, beverage bottling, laboratory reagent preparation, and fluid tank capacity sizing. One cup (us customary) equals 236.588237 milliliters, while 1 milliliter equals 0.004227 cups (us). Whether you are verifying volume & liquid specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many milliliters (mL) are in 1 cup (us customary) (cup)?
faqs.answer: There are 236.5882365 milliliters (mL) in 1 cup (us customary) (cup), which rounds to 236.5882 mL for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 milliliter equals 0.004227 cups (us).

faqs.question: How do I convert cups (us) to milliliters (cup to mL)?
faqs.answer: To convert cups (us) to milliliters, use the formula: mL = cup × 236.5882365. For example, converting 0.75 cup gives 177.4412 mL.

faqs.question: What is 0.75 cups (us) in milliliters?
faqs.answer: 0.75 cups (us) (cup) equals exactly 177.4412 milliliters (mL) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
